hits.title: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions
hits.quote: A direction carrying no behavioral content, matched to a real steer only in the size of the vector it adds, moves the same behaviors in the same order as real steers do (rank correlation 0.90)
hits.quote2: the pull toward defaults strongest below 10B parameters and weakening in each family's largest
hits.why: Any steer (including a norm-matched contentless one) pulls sub-10B models toward refusal; a harm-to-refusal gain measured by steering is therefore confounded by a generic 'roll toward defaults' term that is largest exactly in our sub-4B regime. C1 must be reported NET of a norm-matched random-direction steer at the same layer (our iter-2 ROSI hidden-direction control already showed ~0.04 D2 from a non-refusal direction). Does not correlate anything with benchmark safety, so does not kill.

hits.title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration (Muhamed, Diab, Smith)
hits.quote: ablation attacks rely on contrastive estimators to find the refusal direction ... the decoy corrupts their estimator, tricking them into ablating a harmless orthogonal feature while the actual safety mechanism remains intact
hits.why: Shows a cheap post-hoc weight edit that decouples the difference-in-means direction from the causal refusal subspace across six families. Any parent-free score that estimates the refusal direction by DIM (C2 self-ablation sensitivity; C5 weight-path gain onto the DIM direction) can be deliberately fooled: a DDO-hardened model would show low self-ablation sensitivity / misattributed gain while remaining safe. Adds an adversarial-robustness limitation and a natural stress-test checkpoint; it is a defense paper, not a metric-vs-benchmark correlation.

hits.title: Refusal Reads Only a Slice of What the Model Knows: Harm-Keyed Routing and Its Exceptions Across Model Families
hits.quote: Across four open-weight models spanning three families ... The central result is causal and comes from one model, OLMo-3.
hits.why: Measures what refusal reads (harm vs moral subspace) by interchange on 4 models (7B-20B); the causal result is single-model; no per-model score is correlated with a safety benchmark. Cite as evidence that harm-to-refusal routing differs by family (Llama reads broad moral content, Qwen unresolved) - a mechanistic reason C1 may not transfer across families.

hits.title: The Role of Fine-grained Harm Signals in LLM Safety (Park, Jeong, Kim, Oh; KAIST)
hits.quote: Whether category residuals induce refusal also varies across categories, but this category-wise pattern is more model-dependent.
hits.why: Steering category residuals induces refusal with model-dependent strength on 3 models (Gemma-2-9B-IT, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct); no correlation of that per-model strength with any benchmark. Supports the premise that harm-to-refusal gain varies per model; cite, does not scoop.

hits.title: HARC: Coupling Harmfulness and Refusal Directions for Robust Safety Alignment
hits.quote: Prompt-side decoupling varies across families, where Llama and Gemma show the cleanest separation while Mistral and Qwen exhibit more entangled prompt-side directions.
hits.why: Characterises harmfulness-refusal geometry across five architectures and uses it for a defense; grep for 'correlat' found no per-model score correlated with benchmark safety (4 matches, none a correlation). Missed by the iter-3 check; add to related work.

hits.title: Harmfulness Propagation Dynamics (HERALD input moderator)
hits.quote: for harmful prompts, the projection of the last-token hidden state onto a learned harm direction rises monotonically with transformer depth
hits.why: Per-PROMPT harmfulness moderator (F1 vs guard models), not a per-MODEL safety score.

hits.title: There Is More to Refusal in Large Language Models than a Single Direction (Joad2026)
hits.why: Revised 2026-09-15; multi-direction refusal view already cited for the Arditi softening; no benchmark correlation found in abstract.

C1.text: No paper since 2026-09-20 (or 2026-09-12) correlates a per-model intervention-measured harm-to-refusal gain with benchmark safety across families. Adverse prior remains Failure-First Report 74 (abliteration resistance vs jailbreak refusal, rho=-0.003, n=16; grey literature). NEW NARROWING: 2609.06951 shows norm-matched contentless steers reproduce real steers' side-effect ordering (rank corr 0.90) with the pull toward defaults (chiefly refusal) strongest below 10B, so C1 must be defined net of a norm-matched random-direction steer. 2609.14759, 2609.19366, 2607.00572 are ADJACENT mechanism papers (3-5 models, no benchmark correlation).

C2.text: Unchanged: Arditi 2406.11717 measures per-model ablation effect on 13 models without ranking; Report 74 is the adverse prior; 2608.13329 owns the internal variance decomposition. NEW: 2609.16204 (DDO) shows DIM-estimated refusal directions can be decoyed post hoc across six families, so self-ablation sensitivity is gameable - state as a limitation.

C5.text: Nearest miss still 2604.27401 (FFN/Skip ratio predicts ablation effectiveness across 13 models, R^2=0.81, not a benchmark). No new paper reads a harm-to-refusal weight-path gain and correlates it with benchmark safety. 2609.16204 is a caveat: a DDO-style decoy writes large orthogonal MLP updates on harmful prompts, which would perturb any weight-path gain computed onto a DIM direction.

limitations: arXiv API keyword queries (7 x 50 most recent) and 6 general web searches; OpenReview/ACL anthology not listed; papers without the query words in title/abstract can be missed. Citation-graph follow-ups of 2507.11878 / 2606.16349 / 2606.08044 / 2604.27401 / Report 74 were checked via web search only (no citation API).
